Let $I$ be an open time interval in seconds and let $\Omega=\prod_{j=1}^3(\mathbb R/L_j\mathbb Z)$, with fixed periods $L_j>0$ in metres. Give $\Omega$ the completed, unnormalised pushforward of Lebesgue measure on $C=\prod_{j=1}^3[0,L_j)$ under the quotient map, as in the kinetic-density definition. Let $f:\Omega\times\mathbb R^3\times I\to(0,\infty)$ be $C^1$ in $(x,t)$ and $C^2$ in $v$, with $v$ measured in metres per second and $f$ in the units assigned by the kinetic-density definition. Fix a constant $f_{\rm ref}>0$ with the same units as $f$. Put $\ell=\log(f/f_{\rm ref})$, $A=f(x,v,t)f(x,w,t)$, and $B=f(x,v',t)f(x,w',t)$. Use the elastic collision set $Q_{\rm el}=\{(v,w,v',w')\in\mathbb R^{12}:v+w=v'+w',\ |v|^2+|w|^2=|v'|^2+|w'|^2\}$ with its relative Borel sigma-algebra and the nonnegative countably additive measure $\nu$ invariant under particle exchange in either pair and incoming/outgoing interchange, together with the weak operator $Q_\nu$ from the elastic-collision definition. Assume for each $t$ that $f$, $f|v|^2$, and $f|\ell|$ are integrable over $\Omega\times\mathbb R^3$. On each compact time interval assume a common integrable envelope in $(x,v)$ for $|(1+\ell)\partial_t f|$; at each $t$ assume $(1+|\ell|)|v\cdot\nabla_x f|$ is integrable over $\Omega\times\mathbb R^3$. In addition, assume
$$f(1+|v|)|\ell|,\quad (1+|\ell|)|\partial_t f|,\quad (1+|\ell|)|v|\,|\nabla_x f|\in L^1_{\rm loc}(I\times\Omega\times\mathbb R^3,dt\,dx\,dv),$$
so the entropy density, entropy flux, and local differentiation terms are integrable on compact time-space regions. Define
$$D(x,t):=\frac14\int_{Q_{\rm el}}(A-B)\log(A/B)\,d\nu.$$
Assume that $D$ is measurable and locally integrable on $I\times\Omega$, and that for each $t$ its spatial section belongs to $L^1(\Omega)$. At every $(x,t)$ assume $f(x,\cdot,t)\in\mathcal D_\nu$ and $1,\ell(x,\cdot,t)\in\mathcal S_{f(x,\cdot,t)}$, with the measurability and absolute-convergence conditions of the elastic-collision definition. With $\delta\varphi=\varphi(v)+\varphi(w)-\varphi(v')-\varphi(w')$, assume
$$\int_{\mathbb R^3}\varphi(v)Q_\nu(f)(v)\,dv=\frac14\int_{Q_{\rm el}}(B-A)\delta\varphi\,d\nu$$
for those two tests, and suppose $\partial_t f+v\cdot\nabla_x f=Q_\nu(f)$. Define
$$h(x,t):=\int_{\mathbb R^3}f\log(f/f_{\rm ref})\,dv,\qquad J_H(x,t):=\int_{\mathbb R^3}v f\log(f/f_{\rm ref})\,dv,$$
$$H(t):=\int_\Omega h(x,t)\,dx,\qquad D_{\rm tot}(t):=\int_\Omega D(x,t)\,dx.$$
Then the local entropy balance holds in distributions: for every $\eta\in C_c^\infty(I\times\Omega)$,
$$\int_I\int_\Omega\bigl(h\,\partial_t\eta+J_H\cdot\nabla_x\eta-D\eta\bigr)\,dx\,dt=0.$$
Moreover, $D(x,t)\ge0$ for almost every $(x,t)$. The periodic global entropy $H$ is differentiable and
$$\frac{dH}{dt}=-D_{\rm tot}(t)\le0.$$
The inequality is conditional on the adopted weak collision identity; it is not a derivation from reversible many-particle mechanics or a kinetic-PDE existence theorem.
$$\partial_t h+\nabla_x\cdot J_H=-D$$
$$h=\int_{\mathbb R^3}f\log(f/f_{\rm ref})\,d^3v,\qquad J_H=\int_{\mathbb R^3}v f\log(f/f_{\rm ref})\,d^3v,\qquad s_{\rm kin}=-k_Bh,\qquad j_{\rm kin}=-k_BJ_H.$$
These equations and the incoming factorization are physical model postulates, not deductions.

Let $f_0:\mathbb R^3\to[0,\infty)$ be a finite-valued measurable velocity density with units fixed by the kinetic-density definition, with $\int\omega_3f_0\,dv<\infty$, number density $n>0$, and strictly positive centered second moment. Let $M=M[f_0]$ be its positive-temperature Gaussian from the single-species BGK definition. Fix a constant reference density $f_{\rm ref}>0$ with the same units as $f_0$ and assume $\int f_0|\log(f_0/f_{\rm ref})|\,dv<\infty$, with $0\log0:=0$ and the integrand $f_0|\log(f_0/f_{\rm ref})|$ assigned value zero where $f_0=0$. Define
$$f^\epsilon(t,v):=M(v)+e^{-t/(\epsilon\tau)}(f_0(v)-M(v)),\qquad t\ge0\text{ in seconds}.$$
Then $f^\epsilon\ge0$, has the same mass, momentum, and kinetic energy as $f_0$ for every $t$, belongs to $C^1([0,\infty);L^1(\omega_3\,dv))$, and solves, as an equality in $L^1(\omega_3\,dv)$,
$$\partial_t f^\epsilon=\frac{M[f^\epsilon]-f^\epsilon}{\epsilon\tau},\qquad f^\epsilon(0)=f_0.$$
A solution means a nonnegative $C^1([0,\infty);L^1(\omega_3\,dv))$ function satisfying this equality at each time. The solution is unique among nonnegative solutions in this function class whose density and temperature remain strictly positive. Moreover,
$$\int_{\mathbb R^3}\omega_3|f^\epsilon(t)-M|\,dv =e^{-t/(\epsilon\tau)}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\omega_3|f_0-M|\,dv,$$
and for every $T_*>0$,
$$\int_0^{T_*}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\omega_3|f^\epsilon-M|\,dv\,dt \le\epsilon\tau\int_{\mathbb R^3}\omega_3|f_0-M|\,dv.$$

derivations.claim: Let $C=n_0/(8V_c^3)$ and $R=\sqrt3V_c/v_*$. The cube has volume $8V_c^3$, so $\int f_0\,d^3v=n_0$. Symmetry of each interval gives $\int v f_0\,d^3v=0$. For the second moment, each coordinate contributes $(2V_c)^2\int_{-V_c}^{V_c}s^2\,ds=8V_c^5/3$, so $\int_{[-V_c,V_c]^3}|v|^2\,d^3v=8V_c^5$; dividing by $8V_c^3$ gives mean square speed $V_c^2$. Thus $\int |v|^2f_0\,d^3v=n_0V_c^2=3n_0k_BT_0/m$, so the mean velocity is zero and its temperature is $T_0$. On the support, $\omega_3(v)\le1+R+R^2+R^3$, hence $\int\omega_3 f_0\,d^3v\le n_0(1+R+R^2+R^3)<\infty$. With $f_{\rm ref}>0$ in the same units as $C$, $\int f_0|\log(f_0/f_{\rm ref})|\,d^3v=n_0|\log(C/f_{\rm ref})|<\infty$, using $0\log0=0$.

The Maxwellian $M$ is strictly positive on all of $\mathbb R^3$, whereas $f_0$ vanishes outside the compact cube, so $f_0\ne M$ almost everywhere and $\|f_0-M\|_{1,3}>0$. The data in step 1.1 satisfy the hypotheses of [F1]; applying it gives the exact solution and exponential weighted-norm equality.

For each fixed $t>0$, $e^{-t/(\varepsilon\tau)}\to0$ as $\varepsilon\to0$, so the equality in step 2.1 gives $f^\varepsilon(t)\to M$ in weighted $L^1$. At $t=0$, the solution is $f_0$, whose positive mismatch was proved in step 2.1. The initial layer is therefore a conditional model prediction for this hypothetical preparation, not an empirical result.
